verdict: NETWORK COMPLETION (complete_network.py): the curated network and the measured knockout edges merged into one typed graph, with every measured edge accounted for. The merged object has 57,696 curated regulatory edges, 192,784 curated physical edges and 21,228 measured directed edges (8,726 specific) over 337 usable source knockouts. ROUTING: on the combined curated graph 6,172/8,726 specific measured edges (71%) can be reached within 4 hops and 2,554 cannot. THAT 71% IS NOT THE RESULT, AND READING IT AS ONE WOULD BE THE WHOLE MISTAKE. The curated graph is dense enough to reach almost anything, so every route was scored against a DEGREE-MATCHED DECOY looked up in the same BFS, over all 5 decoy replicates: REGULATORY layer reaches only 8% of measured edges but the real target is strictly closer than its decoy in 55.8% of decisive pairs (p=3.4e-07); COMBINED layer reaches only 71% of measured edges but the real target is strictly closer than its decoy in 53.1% of decisive pairs (p=1.6e-12). THE NULL'S COVARIATE DECIDED THIS AND I GOT IT WRONG FIRST TIME: an earlier version bucketed decoys on mover-frequency alone and called it degree-matched. Mover-frequency correlates with curated-graph degree at rho~0.01, so it matched nothing relevant to a claim about graph DISTANCE, and under it the combined layer came out at chance (50.2%, p=0.82) -- a false negative I was about to publish. Matching on log2(in-degree in the routing layer) x mover-frequency brings the balance to mean in-degree 68 vs 68 and reachable-at-all 71% vs 71%, and the combined layer then beats chance. Both layers do. The decomposition also matters: REGULATORY 75% of decisive pairs are settled by true distance rather than by one side simply being unreachable; COMBINED 97% of decisive pairs are settled by true distance rather than by one side simply being unreachable. THE DEPTH PROFILE SAYS WHERE THE NETWORK STOPS EXPLAINING, and it is the single most useful number here: enrichment over matched decoys by route length is direct 1.91x, 1 intermediate 1.04x, 2 intermediates 0.97x, 3 intermediates 0.95x on the combined layer (and direct 1.00x, 1 intermediate 1.32x on the regulatory layer). Direct curated edges are genuinely enriched among measured effects, one regulatory intermediate still carries signal, and BY TWO INTERMEDIATES THE ROUTES ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A RANDOM WALK. So the network can be completed, but it can only be TRUSTED one hop out -- which is why the long explanatory chains this project kept constructing dissolved under test. SIGN: UNTESTABLE -- only 7 of 8,726 specific measured edges have a signed curated counterpart at all, so the activator/repressor logic cannot be scored here; the curated regulatory layer barely intersects the knockouts usable as sources. VALUE, the only non-circular test: sources split 70/30, completion built from TRAIN sources only, held-out specific-mover recall@50 is 0.025 for the curated network alone and 0.030 for the completed network (+0.006; random 0.007). That gain is NOT distinguishable from noise -- it helps on 19/98 held-out sources and hurts on 0 (paired Wilcoxon p=0.12). AND THE SCALE SETTLES IT, AGAINST A REFERENCE COMPUTED IN THIS SETUP RATHER THAN AN IMPORTED ONE: quoting this project's familiar 0.26 tide-null and 0.49 best-model here would be a cross-metric comparison, since those come from the harness (pkl, TAU=1.0) and this module scores the uncensored parquet at |z|>=4.2 with a different tide definition. Recomputed on exactly these sources and this truth definition, simply ranking genes by how often they move under ANY knockout -- the tide-null, which uses no network at all -- scores 0.143, versus 0.030 for the completed network. So the completed graph is roughly 5x WORSE than ignoring the network entirely and predicting the generic response. Completing the network and walking it is not a route to prediction. JOINTS, and these ARE enriched: REGULATORY 5 of 56 genes carrying >=5 routes reach z>=2 against 5 null replicates (chance ~1); COMBINED 81 of 545 genes carrying >=5 routes reach z>=2 against 5 null replicates (chance ~19). The chance expectation there is EMPIRICAL, not a normal tail: a z built from 5 replicates with a Poisson floor is not normal, so the count of genes clearing z>=2 when one replicate is held out and scored against the other four IS the chance count for this estimator. Note what joints do and do not show: they ask which intermediates routes pass through, not whether targets are closer. A knockout's real targets are a coherent set, so their routes CONVERGE on shared intermediates more than independently-drawn decoys do even at identical distances. Convergence is real but it is a property of the target set, not evidence that the curated path is the mechanism. AND THE NAMES DO NOT SURVIVE SCRUTINY, WHICH IS THE HONEST HEADLINE OF THIS SECTION. BFS records one parent per node, so wherever several equally-short paths exist -- the common case at median degree 15 -- the credited intermediate is decided by the order neighbours are visited, which is alphabetical and arbitrary. Permuting that order retains only Jaccard 0.42 of the joint set. So the COUNT is a result (there is more convergence than chance) but WHICH GENES ARE NAMED is largely an implementation artifact, and the ranked table should be read as a weak shortlist, not as identified mechanism. Recovering real joints needs credit distributed over ALL shortest paths (Brandes-style), which this module does not do. For what it is worth under that caveat, AND AGAINST BASE RATES rather than quoted bare: 4/5 of the significant regulatory joints are annotated transcription factors (background among scoreable genes 78%), and 5/5 were never knocked out in this panel -- but so were 100% of ALL scoreable genes, so that second number is the panel's composition rather than a property of the joints, and I am not going to present it as a finding. They include haematopoietic regulators plausible for K562 (RUNX1, HHEX) alongside broadly-studied factors with large curated regulons (MYCN, ESR2, CASP3). Deterministic; degree-matched decoys throughout, joints z-scored against replicated nulls with a Poisson variance floor, and restricted to genes carrying >=5 routes so that a gene whose few null replicates happen to agree cannot be handed an infinite z.
